explanation: Until 1992 the Summer and Winter Games fell in the same year. The IOC then staggered them so that an Olympics would be held every two years.

claims.text: The 1994 Winter Olympics in Lillehammer were held two years after the 1992 Winter Olympics in Albertville.
Albertville 1992, Nagano 1998 and Calgary 1988 each came four years after the previous Winter Games.
From 1924 to 1992 the Winter and Summer Olympics were held in the same years.
The IOC staggered the Summer and Winter Games so that an Olympics would be held every two years.

claimResults.note: From 1994 the Winter and Summer rows alternate every two years (1994 W, 1996 S, 1998 W, 2000 S and so on to 2026 W). That the IOC chose this on purpose rests on knowledge.

claimResults.note: 1994 is the first Winter year without Summer Games.

evidence.restatement: The IOC voted in 1986 to put the Winter Games on their own cycle, two years off the Summer Games, starting with 1994.
